title: The pavilion
logline: Monday. The glass pavilion itself, in fog, a daily of a building: four panels, the fog moving on the glass, Wood's reflection in it once.

panels.composition: A glass pavilion on a lawn above the water, fog on the glass outside, string lights inside, figures moving. Razor-sharp architecture. WOOD's reflection faint in one pane.

image.prompt: a modern glass pavilion on a lawn above dark water in fog with string lights and figures inside, drawn with pristine architectural line, a thin man's faint reflection in one pane, razor-sharp ink

panels.composition: One pane: fog condensing, a hand inside wiping a circle clear, a face in the circle looking out — a guest, not him.

characters.pose: wiping a circle in the fogged glass

image.prompt: close-up of a fogged glass pane with a hand inside wiping a clear circle and a stranger's face looking out through it

panels.composition: The pavilion from the dock below, the whole glass box lit like an aquarium on the hill, the fog around it.

image.prompt: a lit glass pavilion on a hill seen from a dock below at night in fog, glowing like an aquarium, no words

panels.composition: Same. The lights going off inside, one string at a time. The glass going dark. The fog the same.

image.prompt: the same glass pavilion with its string lights going out and the glass going dark in fog, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: A daily of a building. His reflection once.
